In the 2.5 years since OpenAI debuted ChatGPT, the number of large language models (LLMs) that the company has made available as options to power its hit chatbot has steadily grown.
In fact, there are now a total of 7 (!!!) different AI models that paying ChatGPT subscribers (of the $20 Plus tier and more expensive tiers) can choose between when interacting with the trusty chatbot — each with its own strengths and weaknesses.
These include:
GPT-4o
o3
o4-mini
o4-mini-high
GPT-4.5 (Research Preview)
GPT-4.1
GPT-4.1-mini
But how should a user decide
which one
to use for their particular prompt, question, or task? After all, you can only pick one at a time.
The AI Impact Series Returns to San Francisco - August 5
The next phase of AI is here - are you ready? Join leaders from Block, GSK, and SAP for an exclusive look at how autonomous agents are reshaping enterprise workflows - from real-time decision-making to end-to-end automation.
Secure your spot now - space is limited:
https://bit.ly/3GuuPLF
Is help on the way?
Help appears to be on the way imminently from OpenAI — as reports emerged over the last few days on X from AI influencers, including OpenAI’s own researcher “
Roon
(
@tszzl on X
)” (speculated to be technical team member Tarun Gogineni) — of a new “router” function that will automatically select the best OpenAI model to respond to the user’s input on the fly, depending on the specific input’s content.
As Roon posted on the social network X yesterday, July 20, 2025, in since-deleted response to influencer Lisan al Gaib’s statement that they “don’t want a model router I want to be able to select the models I use”:
“You’ll still be able to select. This is a product to make sure that doctors aren’t stuck on 4o-mini”
Similarly, Yuchen Jin, Co-founder & CTO of AI inference cloud provider Hyperbolic Labs,
wrote in an X post on July 19.
“
Heard GPT-5 is imminent, from a little bird.
It’s not one model, but multiple models. It has a router that switches between reasoning, non-reasoning, and tool-using models.
That’s why Sam said they’d “fix model naming”: prompts will just auto-route to the right model.
GPT-6 is in training.
I just hope they’re not delaying it for more safety tests. :)
“
While a presumably far more advanced GPT-5 model would (and will) be huge news if and when released, the router may make life much easier and more intelligent for the average ChatGPT subscriber.
It would also follow on the heels of other third-party products such as the web-based
Token Monster chatbot
, which automatically select and combine responses from multiple third-party LLMs to respond to user queries.
Asked about the router idea and comments from “Roon,” an OpenAI spokesperson declined to provide a response or further information at this time.
Solving the overabundance of choice problem
To be clear, every time OpenAI has released a new LLM to the public, it has diligently shared in either a blog post or release notes or both what it thinks that particular model is good for and designed to help with.
For example, OpenAI’s “o” series reasoning models — o3, o4-mini, o4-mini high — have performed better on math, science, and coding tests thanks to benchmarking tests, while non-reasoning models like the new GPT-4.5 and 4.1 seem to do better at creative writing and communications tasks.
Dedicated AI influencers and power users may understand very well what all these different models are good and not so good at.
But regular users who don’t follow the industry as closely, nor have the time and finances available to test them all out on the same input prompts and compare the outputs, will understandably struggle to make sense of the bewildering array of options.
That could mean they’re missing out on smarter, more intelligent, or more capable responses from ChatGPT for their task at hand. And in the case of fields like medicine, as Roon alluded to, the difference could be one of life or death.
It’s also interesting to speculate on how an automatic LLM router might change public perceptions toward and adoption of AI more broadly.
ChatGPT
already counted 500 million active users as of March
. If more of these people were automatically guided toward more intelligent and capable LLMs to handle their AI queries, the impact of AI on their workloads and that of the entire global economy would seem likely to be felt far more acutely, creating a positive “snowball” effect.
That is, as more people saw more gains from ChatGPT
automatically
choosing the right AI model for their queries, and as more enterprises reaped greater efficiency from this process, more and more individuals and organizations would likely be convinced by the utility of AI and be more willing to pay for it, and as they did so, even
more
AI-powered workflows would spread out in the world.
But right now, this is pr

data.title: FCC to eliminate gigabit speed goal and scrap analysis of broadband prices
data.author: mikece
data.article_summary: 美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）正在放弃拜登时代用于衡量宽带部署进展的标准。FCC主席布伦丹·卡尔（Brendan Carr）的提案将改变评估方式，即使宽带未达到100%部署，行业也能获得通过评级。该提案取消了千兆宽带速度的长期目标，也不再跟踪宽带的 affordability（可负担性）。卡尔主张聚焦于宽带是否“正在部署”，而非是否已经完成部署，并认为这样能提供更多有用信息。此外，提案还提到不再考虑“可负担性”和“采用率”等标准，回归法律文本的字面解释。此前，拜登时期的FCC曾试图扩展价格数据的分析，但未有实质进展。

The Federal Communications Commission is ditching Biden-era standards for measuring progress toward the goal of universal broadband deployment.
The changes will make it easier for the FCC to give the broadband industry a passing grade in an annual progress report. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr's proposal would give the industry a thumbs-up even if it falls short of 100 percent deployment, eliminate a long-term goal of gigabit broadband speeds, and abandon a new effort to track the affordability of broadband.
Section 706 of the Telecommunications Act
requires
the FCC to determine whether broadband is being deployed "on a reasonable and timely basis" to all Americans. If the answer is no, the US law says the FCC must "take immediate action to accelerate deployment of such capability by removing barriers to infrastructure investment and by promoting competition in the telecommunications market."
Generally, Democratic-led commissions have found that the industry isn't doing enough to make broadband universally available, while Republican-led commissions have found the opposite. Democratic-led commissions have also periodically increased the speeds used to determine whether advanced telecommunications capabilities are widely available, while Republican-led commissioners have kept the speed standards the same.
No focus on broadband affordability
Carr's
proposal
, which was released on Thursday and is scheduled for a
vote on August 7
, criticized the previous administration's approach. Carr intends to focus the next FCC inquiry on the statute's "is being deployed" phrase rather than looking at whether broadband has already been deployed. Carr's proposal said:
To further realign our section 706 inquiry with the statute's plain language, we intend to focus our inquiry on whether advanced telecommunications capability "is being deployed," rather than whether it already has been deployed, as was the focus of the 2024 Report. We believe that the prior Report's binary interpretation of the threshold for issuing a passing or failing grade in the ultimate section 706 finding effectively read the "reasonable and timely" language out of the statute. That interpretation seemingly found anything short of 100% was insufficient to warrant a passing grade and thus disregarded Congress's use of the present progressive tense in "is being deployed." Moreover, we believe that assessing the progress at which advanced telecommunications capability is being deployed would provide far more—and more helpful—information to Congress and the public than an overly simplistic inquiry into whether or not 100% of Americans already have access to such capability.
Carr also doesn't want the FCC to investigate "extraneous" matters such as whether broadband is cheap enough to be affordable.
"The Commission in the 2024 Report departed from the way that the section 706 inquiry had historically been conducted by for the first time reading several extraneous universal service criteria into the section 706 statutory inquiry based upon its interpretation of Congressional intent. We propose to reorient the section 706 inquiry back to the plain language of the statute and eliminate this expansion," the Carr proposal says.
A footnote indicating which extraneous material will be removed said the 2024 report "for the first time incorporated the universal service goals of deployment, adoption, affordability, availability, and equitable access to broadband throughout the United States as the metrics for conducting the section 706 inquiry." Carr objected to the use of words like "affordability" and "adoption" when the 2024 report was released, saying, "those terms appear nowhere in Section 706."
The Carr FCC's proposal points to a
Supreme Court ruling
that limited the ability of federal agencies to interpret ambiguous laws. Given that ruling, "we believe it is most prudent to strictly adhere to the statutory text," the proposal said.
The Biden-era FCC didn't get very far in analyzing broadband prices. Former Chairwoman Jessica Rosenworcel, who led the FCC under Biden, wanted to expand the commission's use of pricing data. An
FCC inquiry in September 2024
sought comment on how the FCC could add more pricing data to its annual analysis, noting that the March 2024 report lacked "granular price information, especially for rural areas, limited the analysis to overall patterns of affordability."
Scrapping long-term gigabit goal
The most recent Section 706 report,
released in March 2024
after a 3–2 vote, also
raised the FCC's Internet speed benchmark
to 100Mbps download speeds and 20Mbps upload speeds. The previous benchmark of 25Mbps downstream and 3Mbps upstream had been in place for nine years.

data.title: NONOS: Open-source, privacy-first Sonos alternative that actually sounds good
data.author: napowderly
data.article_summary: NONOS是一款开源智能音箱，主打高端音质和隐私保护，硬件设计通过.ato文件声明。其主要特点包括：双驱动音频系统，采用德州仪器TAS5825M放大器和ADI ADAU145x DSP，支持无损播放。核心计算模块为Raspberry Pi CM5，具备千兆以太网和USB-C供电支持。音箱支持Spotify、AirPlay和蓝牙等多种流媒体服务，并可通过触控界面和手势控制。音频处理管道从CM5开始，经过I2S、DSP到放大器，最后输出到扬声器。项目硬件设计文件采用.ato格式，包含主板和控制模块的设计，整体结构包括电子、固件、机械设计和文档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕硬件和软件工具的功能、开放性以及具体应用的讨论，包括对DSP开放性的关注、对特定硬件设计工具的兴趣，以及对Sonos扬声器设计的不解。

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind] 对Analog Devices的ADAU145x DSP芯片如何使用非常感兴趣，认为DSP领域对开放源代码和知识共享有较大的抵触。他提到，尽管声音工程的数学基础是公开的，但该领域仍然封闭。他还希望有一个像Open Screen Protocol这样的协议，可以用于投屏功能，并认为在设备中加入Raspberry Pi（树莓派）是可行的。此外，他对"atopile"这个硬件设计工具感到好奇，认为将代码转换为Kicad设计的想法很酷，尤其是在可重用性方面有潜力。

• [iopapa] 对Sonos扬声器设计提出质疑，不理解为什么Sonos在扬声器中配置了高音单元（tweeter），但在主链路设置中却几乎将其关闭。他猜测这可能与消费者对"缺乏高音 = 优质声音"的认知有关，暗示这种设计可能是基于市场调研或焦点测试的结果。

补充讨论：
• [jauntywundrkind] 提到了具体的技术资源，如Open Screen Protocol的链接和atopile工具的文档及相关讨论链接（来自Hacker News），展示了其对具体技术细节和社区讨论的关注。
• [iopapa] 的评论更侧重于对Sonos产品设计选择的质疑，未深入讨论技术细节，而是从用户体验和市场角度提出看法。

争议焦点：

data.title: Earth will spin faster on July 22 to create 2nd-shortest day in history
data.author: dangle1
data.article_summary: 地球将在2025年7月22日经历一个比平常短1.34毫秒的昼夜周期，成为有记录以来最短的一天之一。尽管这种变化微小到难以察觉，但它属于近年来地球自转速度加快的一个趋势。自2020年以来，地球多次打破自转速度记录，最短的一天出现在2024年7月5日，比正常短1.66毫秒。科学家预测2025年7月9日、7月22日和8月5日可能是当年最短的几天。这种加速现象的原因尚不完全明确，但有研究指出可能与极地冰融化、海平面上升以及地球内部液核的运动有关。尽管加速趋势可能正在放缓，但科学家预测地球自转未来可能再次减速。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44641561.article_content:
(Image credit: joecicak/Getty Images)
Earth will complete a full rotation in slightly less time than usual on Tuesday, July 22, making it one of the shortest days ever recorded.
The difference will be just 1.34 milliseconds less than the standard
24 hours
— not something you'll notice — but it's part of a puzzling trend in Earth's rotational behavior that has been unfolding in recent years. If it continues, a second may need to be subtracted from atomic clocks around 2029 — a so-called negative leap second, which has never been done before.
The s
peed of Earth's rotation
isn't fixed. Long ago, a day was much shorter than the 24 hours — or 86,400 seconds — we're now accustomed to. According to a 2023
study
, a day on Earth was approximately 19 hours for a significant part of Earth's early history, due to a balance between solar atmospheric tides and lunar ocean tides. However, over deep time, a day on Earth has become consistently longer. The primary culprit has been tidal friction from the moon, which has caused it to gradually move farther away from Earth. As it moves away, the moon saps Earth's rotational energy, causing Earth's rotation to slow and days to lengthen.
You may like
Did you feel it? Earth just had one of its shortest days ever and 2 more are coming
Summer solstice 2025 brings changing seasons to Earth on June 20
Earth is farthest from the sun today. So why is it so hot?
So why the sudden reverse?
From when records began (with the invention of the atomic clock) in 1973 until 2020, the shortest day ever recorded was 1.05 milliseconds less than 24 hours, according to
Timeanddate.com
. But since 2020, Earth has repeatedly broken its own speed records. The shortest day ever measured occurred on
July 5, 2024
, when Earth's rotation was completed
1.66 milliseconds
faster than usual.
Looking ahead to 2025, scientists predicted that July 9, July 22, and Aug. 5 could be the shortest days of the year. However, new data suggests that July 10 took the lead as the shortest day so far in 2025, clocking in at 1.36 milliseconds less than 24 hours. On July 22, Earth is expected to complete its spin 1.34 milliseconds early, making it a close runner-up. If current predictions hold, Aug. 5 will be about 1.25 milliseconds shorter than usual, leaving July 22 as the second-shortest day of the year.
Earth just had one of its shortest days ever, with more to come.
(Image credit: Created in Canva by Daisy Dobrijevic)
There are signs the acceleration may be easing. The rate of decrease in day length appears to be slowing, but the underlying cause of the recent rotational changes remains elusive.

One
2024 study
suggested that the melting polar ice and rising sea levels may be influencing Earth's spin. However, rather than driving the acceleration, this redistribution of mass might be moderating it. A more likely culprit is deep below our feet — the slowing of Earth's liquid core, which could be redistributing angular momentum in a way that makes the mantle and crust spin slightly faster.
"The cause of this acceleration is not explained," Leonid Zotov, a leading authority on Earth rotation at Moscow State University, told
Timeanddate.com
. "Most scientists believe it is something inside the Earth. Ocean and atmospheric models don't explain this huge acceleration."
Zotov predicts Earth’s rotation may soon decelerate once again. If he’s right, this sudden speeding-up could prove to be just a temporary anomaly in the planet’s long-term trend toward slower rotation and longer days.

If you're forced to use Windows 11, here's how to steal some of your time back
4
Fight back against Redmond's productivity sinks
Avram Piltch
Mon 21 Jul 2025
//
22:18 UTC
Windows 11 is now the most popular desktop operating system, finally beating Windows 10. But it's also loaded with head-scratching default settings that sap your productivity and treat you like a computer illiterate.
Whether it's hiding vital file information from you or making you see advertisements throughout the UI, Windows seems hell-bent on distracting you from your productivity work. Here are the worst time sinks and how to stop them.
Widget board is like reading the headlines in a supermarket checkout aisle
Microsoft's widget at first looks so innocent. By default, it appears on the left or right side of your taskbar and shows the current weather. But don't be fooled; it's out to steal your attention. Sometimes the widget will change to show promotions such as "Trending videos" from Hallstatt, Austria, or let you know about local traffic when you're just sitting at your desk.
Most distractingly, when you hover over the widget or click on it, you're subjected to a mix of distracting news headlines, some of which are quite schlocky. I'll never forget the time I learned that pigs eat humans "far more often than people expect," or the instances where I read about the man who went to hell and heard the demons playing Rihanna songs there.
Windows Widget Board - Click to enlarge
If you're trying to be productive, even helpful headlines are a time sink. To disable widgets, right-click on your taskbar, select Taskbar Settings, and then toggle Widgets to off.
Lock screen wants you to play Candy Crush
By default, the
Windows 11
lock screen displays what Microsoft calls "Windows Spotlight." This is an ad promoting some other Microsoft service, which could be Copilot, Windows Backup, or even a free-to-play game such as Candy Crush Saga.
These advertisements are designed to distract you from your work and get you to focus on whatever Microsoft is hawking. To make the lock screen ads go away, first navigate to Settings->Personalization->Lock screen. Then select Picture instead of Windows Spotlight under "Personalize your lock screen." Finally, select None under "Lock screen status."
Disable ads on the lock screen - Click to enlarge
Search highlights are a lowlight of your day
The Windows search box is one of the most important navigational tools that the operating system has. More often than not, I use search in lieu of the Start menu to find and launch my favorite applications.
By default, the search box shows promotions for MSN content as well as apps. It even tries to get you to play casual games. On the day I wrote this article, it was advertising World Brain Day content. Just imagine if you just came to the search menu to find a document or launch Microsoft Word and you got waylaid by this cruft, because you were tempted to click or you spent time waiting for the images to draw as you opened the menu.
Windows Search Highlights adds cruft to your search - Click to enlarge
To disable Search highlights, open the Search menu, select Search settings from the … menu and then toggle Show Search Highlights to off.
Open search settings - Click to enlarge
Search gives you Bing results when you just wanted files and apps
The Windows search box not only promotes lame MSN content and games when you first click it, but it also shows you Bing search results, even when you just want to find content on your local drives. For example, I started typing "word" and ended up getting search results for Wordle. Perhaps if I'd had Word installed on the test system, I'd have gotten that instead. Meanwhile, I had to wait while Microsoft downloaded results from Bing.
Searching for word can get you Wordle - Click to enlarge
To disable Windows search suggestions, you'll need to edit the Registry file, so be careful, make sure you have permissions, and back up. In the Registry, navigate to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows. Create a subfolder there called Explorer and enter it. Then create a DWORD (32-bit) Registry called DisableSearchBoxSuggestions and set it to 1.
After your next reboot or relaunch of Explorer, your search suggestions should be gone.

• 观点一：看好软银与OpenAI的合作，认为这是技术与资本的强强联合。支持者认为软银的资金支持与OpenAI的技术实力相结合，有望加速人工智能技术的发展与应用。例子：有人提到软银之前对科技行业的成功投资，如阿里巴巴和Sprint，认为这次合作也可能带来类似的成功。

• 观点二：对合作持谨慎态度，担心资本介入可能会影响OpenAI的初衷。批评者指出，资本的介入可能会导致OpenAI偏离其原本的非营利性和开放性目标，转而追求商业利益。例子：有人提到历史上其他技术公司被大资本收购后失去初心的案例，认为OpenAI应保持其独立性和使命。

• 观点三：关注合作的具体细节和执行情况。有评论者表示，合作的成败不仅取决于双方的资源和能力，还取决于具体的执行策略和合作模式。例子：有人提出需要关注双方在技术研发、市场推广和利益分配等方面的具体安排。

• 争议焦点在于资本介入是否会影响OpenAI的初衷和使命。部分评论者担心软银的商业目标可能会与OpenAI的非营利性初衷产生冲突。

• 有人关注合作对人工智能行业整体的影响。支持者认为这可能会推动整个行业的发展，带来更多创新和机会；反对者则担心这可能会导致市场垄断和不公平竞争。

• 对软银过往投资记录的评价不一。有人认为软银在科技投资领域有丰富的经验和成功的案例，值得信任；也有人指出软银的一些投资项目并不成功，如WeWork，因此对此次合作的效果持怀疑态度。

44638634.article_content:
Things Of Interest
Blog
ChatSCP
2025-07-21              by
qntm
Prominent OpenAI investor Geoff Lewis
may be facing a conspiracy theory-related mental health episode brought about by extended conversations with ChatGPT
.
I found this article to be very interesting. From my perspective, the most interesting angle here is the fact that ChatGPT is obviously just spinning SCP-esque containment documentation at Lewis.
The SCP project has had problems with readers taking its content too seriously since its inception. It's not for nothing that the very first question in
the project's FAQ
is,
Is SCP real?
and the answer to that question is,
No.
It's just that, historically, the people who suffer from this kind of problem, of being unable to discern authentic reality from fiction, have been, you know. Teenagers. Or at least, that's what I've kind of assumed this whole time.
I do not feel comfortable judging Geoff Lewis' mental state from where I'm sitting. Joe Wilkins, the journalist who originally wrote that article, feels similarly:
It's a very delicate thing to try to understand a public figure's mental health from afar.
And I haven't watched
the video
, and I don't really feel that I want to. In fact I find it difficult to even parse
Lewis' Tweets
. So I'm going to refrain from passing judgement there. (And I would prefer it if we avoid that topic in the comments below.)
However: I have read a lot of SCPs over the years. For a few years I used to give pitch critique. And I do feel that I have the authority to state that ChatGPT's effort at creating "original" (?) SCP-esque content is
horrendous, overwritten trash
.
I mean, it
stinks
.
Here is the first of the eight pages of output which Lewis shared:
(The other seven pages can be found starting
here
.)
So:
ChatGPT makes heavy use of long/cool words, reference numbers, Greek letters, codenames, bold text, quotes and bullet points to disguise the fact that this "attestation" is garbled, bordering on incoherent. It reads like mush or fog.
What, for example, the heck is a "sealed internal containment event"? This is not how words are used. Why is "No hallucination. No instability. No recursive entrapment" blockquoted? Who said this? "‍[M]easurable effects on narrative coherence" of what?
What is "vault memory"? How is it "recursive"?
Why is everything recursive?
Why the sudden veer into melodrama with "This is not speculative. This is not metaphor"? What Codex?
These questions are somewhat rhetorical. They could have answers, but that isn't the point.
ChatGPT was borderline certainly trained on the SCP project and has evidently learned how to "borrow" (?) and imitate SCP aesthetics. But ChatGPT wouldn't be the first entity to mistake a genre for its surface level, even within the SCP community. Good fiction in this genre doesn't just throw meaningless, cool-sounding stuff at the reader. The cool-sounding stuff actually has traction. It connects to reality, or at least
a
reality. It has ramifications which actually do provoke thought. There is
substance
. There is
more to it
.
Also: it is not necessary to use an avalanche of grandiose words and codenames and protocols in order to be creepy or scary. There's a point of diminishing returns. The codename "Mirrorthread", for example, is just too much. It's too heavy. The words "mirror" and "thread" metaphorically imply far too many different and unrelated things, and so the combination just means nothing at all...
This stuff is a spice. You can't make the whole dish out of it. A truly solid concept should just work, even if expressed in simple, factual, direct terms. ChatGPT almost fails to express
anything
.
I could guess what the Codex is. I could even construct my own cool idea for what the Codex is, an idea which retconned
The Codex remains structurally intact, sealed, and retrievable by approved fallback protocol.
into a meaningful, even compelling, sentence. But that isn't my job. That would be me meeting ChatGPT well over halfway.
That would be me covering for it.
This would be rejected from the wiki. It would be downvoted heavily. (There is
limitless precedent
. AI content is
banned
on the SCP project.)
Nobody actually likes technobabble. Jargon is better because jargon is meaningful, even if it is arcane and highly specific to an unusual discipline. In both cases we don't know what the words actually mean, but in the second case there is actual substance. And
readers can tell
. And we can tell that the babble in ChatGPT's effort here doesn't signify anything.
Well. I can tell. Geoff Lewis is perhaps having a harder time of it.
*
I'm against AI content on the SCP project. The extremely poor level of quality of AI-generated output is the most obvious objection right now, but actually there are more significant objections here.
For one thing, there are ethical and legal concerns about the way in which ChatGPT was trained. In particular, as I say, it seems like it may well have been trained on the SCP project itself

data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了上海喜马拉雅美术馆的兴衰。该馆由地产大亨戴志康于2005年创立，曾是当代艺术的先锋私营博物馆，后因戴志康金融帝国的崩溃而陷入困境。2019年，戴志康因 financial 犯罪被判19年徒刑，其资产被拍卖，美术馆失去主要资助，逐渐衰败。文章指出，中国许多私营博物馆面临类似困境，常常不正式宣布关闭，而是处于半死不活的状态，给员工和公众带来不确定性。与OCAT等博物馆的沉默处理不同，时代美术馆则较为坦诚地宣布了关闭。文章最后反思了私营文化机构过度依赖个人和商业利益的风险。

44640686.article_content:
Advertisement
Shanghai Himalayas Museum facade, 2025. Photo: Lai Fei
Many private art museums in China are having trouble admitting they no longer exist
Standing in the ruins of the Arata Isozaki-designed Shanghai Himalayas Museum, I feel oddly at ease. It’s less nerve-racking to confront the skeleton of a dead structure than one that’s half-dead but still trying to revive itself. Imagine working here – in its furnished days – clocking in day after day, never knowing for sure if your next paycheque will arrive, or if the upcoming exhibition or programme you’re labouring over is ever going to happen. You’re trapped in a cultural institution that once generated great expectations – both symbolic and economic – and that continues to send out self- and plain deceiving signals of hope that these will be delivered, like the beacon of an airplane that has crashed into a mountainside. It’s a feeling all too familiar to many working in the private museum circuit in China today. You’d likely agree with me (unless you’re running one of these zombie museums): it’s easier to face the dead-dead than the rasping breath of the near-dead who refuse to abandon the slimmest chance of survival.
The Shanghai Himalayas Museum, originally established as the Zendai Museum of Modern Art in 2005 by real-estate magnate Dai Zhikang, was once envisioned as a premier institution for contemporary art. It was, in fact, one of the very first privately funded museums dedicated to contemporary art in China (along with Today Art Museum, founded in Beijing in 2002, and MoCA Shanghai in 2005). In 2012 it relocated to the architecturally ambitious Isozaki-designed Himalayas Center in Pudong, Shanghai. This move was part of Dai’s broader ambition to integrate art, luxury and commerce within a single complex that also housed a hotel, shopping mall and conference centre. In its heyday, the museum hosted exhibitions by the likes of Sean Scully and Michael Craig-Martin; in 2016, it co-organised the inaugural Shanghai Project, a multidisciplinary platform for global discourse, under the co-artistic directorship of Yongwoo Lee, executive director of Shanghai Himalayas Museum at the time, and Hans Ulrich Obrist.
The Shanghai Himalayas Museum’s decline began with the collapse of Dai Zhikang’s financial empire. In 2019 Dai admitted to creating unauthorised capital pools and misappropriating approximately £1 billion in funds from the public, leading to his arrest along with 40 associates. In December 2022 he was sentenced to 19 years in prison, and his assets, including a dilapidated mansion in Shanghai, were auctioned off to repay creditors. The downfall of Dai and the financial instability of the Zendai Group left the Shanghai Himalayas Museum without its primary benefactor. This loss of funding, coupled with the museum’s integration into Dai’s commercial ventures, led to a significant decline in its operations. While it continued to put on sporadic exhibitions (funded by other benefactors or via acts of ‘goodwill’) over the years that followed, a large part of the museum space remained unused and gradually turned into a site of ruin, which, almost uncannily, fulfilled Isozaki’s infamous prophecy that ‘the city of the future lies in ruins’ (which opened his essay for Ryūji Miyamoto’s photobook
Architectural Apocalypse
, published in 1988).
Stored up poster of
Shanghai Project Chapter 2
(2017) curated by Yongwoo Lee and Hans-Ulrich Obrist at Shanghai Himalayas Museum. Photo: Lai Fei
The museum has been inactive since January this year and was cordoned off with an official seal in March. Yet it is likely too soon to conclusively pronounce it dead: in China, the vital signs of a private museum can be more elusive than those of Schrödinger’s cat. You’re never sure when it’s truly dead, or, to quote a famous 1949 poem by Zang Kejia commemorating Lu Xun’s death, ‘some live as though dead; some die yet live forever’.
You would think that the fate of a defunct museum would serve as a cautionary tale about the vulnerabilities of privately funded cultural institutions that rely heavily on individual patrons and commercial interests. But the reality is that if you never announce the death of an institution to (social) media, most people won’t know or care that the institution is no longer active. In China, few museums will officially announce their closure – and there have been countless closures in the past decade. When OCAT Museum Group shut down its Shanghai, Xi’an, Beijing and old Shenzhen branches in 2022, there was an extended period of awkward silence. The decision had been made but no official message or explanation was provided to the general public, leading its directors (whose contracts were terminated) to share their personal words via WeChat moments (which are only visible to contacts). By contrast, the Guangzhou-based Times Museum was refreshingly upfront when it announced the closure of its Berlin space and cessation of Guangzhou’s exhibition program

data.title: Apple details how it trained its new AI models
data.author: mgh2
data.article_summary:
苹果公司在WWDC25上发布了其设备端和云端基础模型的新版本，并在一份技术报告中详细介绍了这些模型的训练、优化和评估过程。报告揭示了几个有趣的细节：

1. **设备端模型的分块设计**：该模型分为两个块，通过这种设计，设备端模型的缓存内存需求减少了37.5%，首 token 输出时间也缩短了37.5%，同时保持了模型的整体性能和输出质量。

2. **云端模型的创新架构**：云端模型采用了名为Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts（PT-MoE）的架构。该架构通过将模型分为多个子网络（专家），仅在相关任务时激活特定专家，提高了响应速度和准确性。

3. **多语言支持大幅提升**：新模型将多语言数据的比例从8%提高到30%，并增加了50%的tokenizer容量，达到15万个token，显著提升了非英语语言的性能。

4. **优化与评估**：苹果详细介绍了模型的优化方法和评估基准，展示了其在性能和效率上的改进。

这份技术报告深入探讨了苹果AI模型的构建细节，展示了其在提高性能和多语言支持方面的努力。

44640561.article_content:
Apple Intelligence
Apple details how it trained its new AI models: 4 interesting highlights
Marcus Mendes
| Jul 21 2025 - 5:58 am PT
2 Comments
During WWDC25, Apple announced new versions of its on-device and cloud-based foundation models. Now, they have published a tech report detailing how those models were trained, optimized, and evaluated. And the report includes some genuinely interesting under-the-hood tidbits.
In a comprehensive document called “
Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models – Tech Report 2025
“, the company walks through multiple aspects of the new models, including their architecture, data sources, pre-training, post-training, tool use development, optimizations, and benchmarks.
Modeling overview for the Apple foundation models. Image:
Apple
It is a very technical, but very worthwhile read if you like to get into the nuts and bolts of this sort of stuff. Here are a few particularly interesting highlights.
The local model was split into two blocks
We already knew that Apple’s on-device model (the one
developers will get to tap into
) has around 3 billion parameters. Now, the company has detailed that this model is actually divided into two blocks:
“Block 1 contains 62.5% of the total transformer layers, while Block 2 contains the remaining 37.5% of the transformer layers, but had the key and value projections removed.”
In practice, this means that the local model requires 37.5% less memory for caching, and the time it takes to output the first token (basically, a fragment of a word) was also cut by about 37.5%. Still, Apple structured the split in a way that it says preserves the model’s overall performance and output quality.
Apple’s on-device vs external models on representative benchmarks. Image:
Apple
As a side note, a few years ago, Apple published
this study
, which looked at swapping parts of an LLM between RAM and flash storage as needed, in order to pack a local model that was bigger than what would otherwise fit on the device’s memory.
While Apple ultimately took a different route, it is interesting to note the different ways the company has been experimenting to offer good local performance, even on memory-constrained devices.
The cloud-based model has a creative architecture
For its server model, Apple built a custom architecture that was tailor-made for its
Private Cloud Compute
platform. It’s called Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts (PT-MoE), and the way it works is pretty neat.
In a nutshell (and at the risk of oversimplifying things), Mixture of Experts is when, instead of relying on one huge AI model, it’s split into smaller subnetworks (or experts) that are only activated when the task is related to something they’re… well, an expert in.
So if your prompt is about cooking, only cooking-related experts are activated, while others remain dormant. The result is still a massive overall model, but its modular design allows it to respond faster (and often more accurately) than if everything were running through the huge, unified model, for every prompt.
Here is an IBM Mixture of Experts explainer, in case you have 8 minutes to spare:
Apple built a new kind of Transformer called the Parallel Track Transformer, then scaled it up with Mixture of Experts (MoE) layers. That sounds way too complicated, but the gist of it is:
Traditional Transformers process tokens through a single stack of layers, one after the other. But rather than using this single-track approach to calculate every token, Apple’s design splits the model into multiple, parallel tracks. Each track processes tokens independently, and only syncs up at certain points.
Then, inside each of those tracks, Apple replaced every other regular transformer layer with an MoE layer, which activates just a few experts for each token, while the rest stay idle. And because each track has its own local experts, the model avoids the processing bottlenecks that happen when everything has to coordinate across the entire system.
Add to that a clever setup that balances local context with big-picture understanding (called Interleaving Global and Local Attention Layers), and the result is a very modular, efficient, and scalable model that’s faster and leaner, but still pretty smart.
Apple increased multilingual representation by 275%
One of the biggest knocks against the initial rollout of Apple Intelligence was (and still is) limited language support beyond English. With its new models, Apple has expanded language support, and the document details the steps it took in order to do that.
According to the document, Apple increased the amount of multilingual data used during training from 8% to 30%. This includes both organic and synthetic content.
Apple also increased its tokenizer (which is basically the model’s token vocabulary) by 50%. This means that its model now knows 150K different tokens, up from the previous 100K.

44640561.article_summary:
苹果公司在WWDC25上发布了其设备端和云端基础模型的新版本，并在一份技术报告中详细介绍了这些模型的训练、优化和评估过程。报告揭示了几个有趣的细节：

1. **设备端模型的分块设计**：该模型分为两个块，通过这种设计，设备端模型的缓存内存需求减少了37.5%，首 token 输出时间也缩短了37.5%，同时保持了模型的整体性能和输出质量。

2. **云端模型的创新架构**：云端模型采用了名为Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts（PT-MoE）的架构。该架构通过将模型分为多个子网络（专家），仅在相关任务时激活特定专家，提高了响应速度和准确性。

3. **多语言支持大幅提升**：新模型将多语言数据的比例从8%提高到30%，并增加了50%的tokenizer容量，达到15万个token，显著提升了非英语语言的性能。

4. **优化与评估**：苹果详细介绍了模型的优化方法和评估基准，展示了其在性能和效率上的改进。

这份技术报告深入探讨了苹果AI模型的构建细节，展示了其在提高性能和多语言支持方面的努力。

data.title: Nine households control 15% of wealth in Silicon Valley as inequality widens
data.author: c420
data.article_summary: 根据圣何塞州立大学发布的《2025年硅谷痛点指数》报告，硅谷的经济不平等问题日益严重。九个家庭掌握了该地区15%的财富，0.1%的居民拥有71%的财富。过去十年，硅谷的财富差距扩大速度是全美的两倍。最富有的九个家庭总财富达6832亿美元，比去年增加1360亿美元。与此同时，11万户家庭几乎无资产。硅谷生活成本高昂，租房需年收入136,532美元。圣何塞在“极度负担不起”的城市中排名第四。54,582户低收入家庭无法负担可负担住房，无家可归者增加了8.2%。种族不平等问题依然存在，拉美裔工人的收入仅为白人同事的33%。尽管企业在多样性和包容性方面作出承诺，但研发部门中只有3%的员工是黑人。不过，报告也提到警察使用武力事件减少和防止无家可归的服务扩展等积极变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：财富不平等及其在特定地区（如硅谷）的影响和原因

不同观点：
• **Aurornis**：认为仅通过计算一个小区域内的财富不平等并不是一个有实际意义的指标。如果那几个最富有的家庭搬走，不平等数据会改善，但实际情况并没有变化。批评者常把财富看作零和游戏，认为富人的财富必然来自于剥夺他人，这种思维加剧了对不平等的愤怒。
  
• **sas224dbm**：指出财富不平等现象不仅限于硅谷，而是全球性问题。富人购买更多资产，中下阶层则需支付租金，这加剧了不平等。引用了"Gary's Economics"的材料来讨论财富不平等的影响。
  
• **atonse**：对财富不平等的统计数据感到困惑，尤其是股票财富如何影响低收入群体。质疑这种不平等是否源于税收问题，以及亿万富翁的数量是否直接影响整个城市的生活成本。
  
• **yonran**：批评“硅谷痛苦指数”将高租金和无家可归问题归咎于9位亿万富翁，认为这是找替罪羊。实际上，问题主要源于当地数以十万计的百万富翁通过监管手段（如分区法）限制多家庭住房的供应。
  
• **seneca**：认为亿万富翁数量少，财富本身是好事，应该鼓励和庆祝，而不是嫉妒和憎恨已经富有的人。

• **yieldcrv**：质疑提高最低工资对解决高租金问题的有效性，认为这种措施不足以帮助低收入者应对高昂的生活成本。

• **foxglacier**：指出富人也是社会的一部分，不能因为财富不平等就把他们隔离起来。贫困问题的根源在于政府政策，而不是富人的存在。

补充讨论：
• **haebom**：质疑批评财富不平等的人是否真的追求平等，还是仅仅因为自己不是亿万富翁而感到不满。
  
• **j_crick**：引用Piketty的观点，暗示财富不平等是一个长期存在的问题，并可能继续存在。

争议焦点：
• 财富不平等的根本原因及其影响：是零和游戏（财富从他人剥夺）还是其他因素（如政府政策、市场力量）导致的不平等。
• 亿万富翁对当地经济和生活成本的实际影响：是否应将高租金和生活成本问题归咎于少数超级富豪。
• 解决财富不平等的有效措施：如提高最低工资是否能有效缓解不平等问题。

44640935.article_content:
Downtown San Jose, California.
Photograph: Steve Proehl/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
Downtown San Jose, California.
Photograph: Steve Proehl/Getty Images
California
Nine households control 15% of wealth in Silicon Valley as inequality widens
Report finds that wealth divide widened in Silicon Valley at double the rate of the whole US over the past decade
Cecilia Nowell
Mon 21 Jul 2025 17.17 EDT
Last modified on Mon 21 Jul 2025 19.16 EDT
Share
Economic inequality has reached a staggering milestone in Silicon Valley: just nine households hold 15% of the region’s wealth, according to new research from San Jose State University. A mere 0.1% of residents hold 71% of the tech hub’s wealth.
The findings come from the 2025 “
Silicon Valley Pain Index
”, a report published by SJSU’s Human Rights Institute each year since 2020. The report aims to quantify “structured inequalities” in Silicon Valley, and measures “pain” as “both personal and community distress or suffering”.
This year’s index reports that the wealth divide has widened in Silicon Valley at double the rate of the whole United States over the past decade. The nine wealthiest households in the valley control $683.2bn – a $136bn increase over the past year.
At the same time, 110,000 households reported nearly none or no assets.
The cost of living in Silicon Valley has risen as well: renters must earn $136,532 to afford an apartment – the highest in the nation.
The report ranked San Jose No 4 in “impossibly unaffordable” cities worldwide (after Hong Kong, Sydney and Vancouver). Yet, no cities in Silicon Valley have raised the minimum wage in the past three years. The report finds that 54,582 low-income households do not have access to an affordable home in San Jose and that homelessness grew 8.2% from 2023.
When they created the Silicon Valley Pain Index in 2020, shortly after the nationwide Black Lives Matter protests, San Jose State University researchers were inspired by the Katrina Pain Index, which aimed to quantify the injustices New Orleans residents faced after Hurricane Katrina. The index continues to show stark racial inequalities.
Hispanic workers in San Jose, Sunnyvale and Santa Clara can expect to make 33 cents for every $1 their white peers take home. And although shareholders have voiced commitments to diversity, equity and inclusion, only 3% of employees working in research and development at Apple are Black (compared with 6% Hispanic/Latino, 36% white and 50% Asian).
Meanwhile, police violence remains a real concern – even years after the Black Lives Matter protests. Ten people died in police custody in the Santa Clara county sheriff’s office in 2024 – the highest in two decades. And San Jose reported five office involved shootings, up three from 2023.
However, the report did note certain improvements in the Silicon Valley area – including a decrease in police use of force incidents in San Jose, an expansion in services to prevent homelessness and environmental sustainability programs.

data.title: Workers at Snopes.com win voluntary recognition
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 2025年7月15日，Snopes.com的员工自愿承认其工会——Snopes Guild，该工会获得了80%员工的支持，代表约10名编辑人员。工会将开始集体谈判以制定合同，目标是确保工作安全性、透明度、现代化工作实践以及公平的薪酬和福利。Snopes管理层自愿承认工会，工会对此表示欢迎，并期待与管理层展开谈判。Snopes成立于1994年，以事实核查闻名，其员工在对抗网络假信息的同时，致力于通过工会改善工作条件。Snopes Guild由Media Guild of the West，Local 39213 of The NewsGuild-CWA代表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工会成立及其代表性

不同观点：
• [支持观点 - philipallstar] 认为工会代表约10个人是新颖的，并提出这些员工可以通过工会集体协商薪资和福利，而不是单独谈判。这暗示了对工会潜在功能的认可和支持。

• [支持观点 - eclecticfrank] 对新工会成立表示欢迎，认为工人自我代表不仅对工人有利，也有助于建立健康和可持续的组织。这一观点强调了工会对组织和工人的双重好处。

• [支持观点 - alwinaugustin] 强烈支持所有公司都应成立工会的想法，表明了对工会普遍存在的积极看法。

• [热烈支持观点 - sneilan1] 对工会成立表示极度赞赏和兴奋，使用“不可思议”和“干得好”等词语表达强烈的正面情感。

• [质疑观点 - drivingmenuts] 对工会仅代表约10名成员的规模表示质疑，认为人数如此少应该能够更精确地确定具体人数。这一评论带有一定的怀疑态度。

• [支持观点 - komali2] 对工会仅10名成员但仍获得自愿承认表示赞赏，认为这是一个了不起的成就。这一观点强调了即使在小规模下，工会的成立也是值得称赞的。

补充讨论：
不同评论之间存在一定的讨论关系，主要集中在工会规模和代表性上。drivingmenuts对工会成员数量的精确性提出质疑，而其他评论多为积极支持工会成立，强调其对工人和组织的潜在好处。争议的焦点在于工会的小规模是否会影响其代表性和效力，但总体上支持声音更为强烈。

44643055.article_content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
July 15, 2025
Media contact:
carrie@mediaguildwest.org
Today, the workers of
Snopes.com
won voluntary recognition of their union, the Snopes Guild.
The union — which secured 80% support before recognition — represents approximately 10 eligible editorial staff members.
With recognition, the Guild will begin the collective bargaining process to develop a contract. Employees are organizing to ensure job security, transparency, modern work practices and fair compensation and benefits.
“We welcome management’s decision to voluntarily recognize the Snopes Guild,” the Snopes Guild organizing committee said. “This is a great step toward creating a fairer workplace for all and we appreciate management’s willingness to engage with us. We look forward to meeting them at the bargaining table.”
Snopes was founded in 1994 and began with investigations into urban legends, hoaxes and folklore. As the publication grew, it became a
signatory
of the International Fact Checking Network in compliance with the organization’s highest standards. Now, Snopes reporters produce complex explainers on celebrity rumors, scientific discoveries and political news — all while combating the day-to-day onslaught of misinformation online.
The Snopes Guild
went public on June 30
and is represented by Media Guild of the West, Local 39213 of The NewsGuild-CWA.
###
About the Snopes Guild
The Snopes Guild is the union of editorial employees at Snopes.com, the oldest and one of the most trusted fact-checking sites on the internet. The Guild is organizing with the Media Guild of the West, Local 39213 of The NewsGuild-CWA. We are committed to upholding the core values of transparency, accuracy and accountability both in our newsroom and our workplace. As the fight against misinformation grows more urgent, we believe the integrity of fact-checking begins with fair conditions for the people who do the work.

data.title: We have made the decision to not continue paying for BBB accreditation
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: CherryTree Computers决定不再支付Better Business Bureau（BBB）的认证费用，因为该认证实际上是企业付费购买的，而非通过良好商业实践赢得的。此前，一个与CherryTree无关的负面投诉被错误地关联到他们的BBB页面，BBB无法或不愿移除该投诉。这使他们质疑BBB认证的实际价值，尤其是在证明企业信誉方面的能力。由于BBB未能解决问题，CherryTree决定终止与其的合作，并通过此文向顾客解释原因。他们相信自己的服务和满意客户的口碑足以证明其信誉，无需依赖任何认证标志。
data.comments_summary:

Why We Have Made The Decision to Not Continue Paying for Accreditation From the Better Business Bureau (BBB)
July 16, 2025
We have made the conscious choice not to continue paying for accreditation from the Better Business Bureau (BBB). We realize that this may raise questions among our customers, and we want to explain why we made this decision.
For years, people have been told to look for BBB accredited businesses, and that it somehow reflects whether a business is on the up and up.
What most don’t realize is that businesses PAY to be accredited with the BBB. You do not EARN an accreditation- you buy it.
A few months ago, an extremely negative complaint and review suddenly appeared under our name registered with the BBB.
It was a person who was upset that a Sting concert was cancelled due to fire. Their complaint was with a Music company that happened to have Cherry Tree in their name, but our business was tagged and reflected poor business practices.
We contacted the BBB many times to ask to please remove this complaint, that was obviously NOT for CherryTree Computers, from our business page.
No one at the BBB was willing or able to assist with our request…because they really don’t have the control or ability to do anything in the event of incorrect information.
This led us to then wonder…. Well, what exactly DOES the BBB do? Why would we continue to pay for accreditation if it only means we get to have the BBB logo on our website, but they don’t actually have the ability to prove or disprove how reputable a company is when it comes to business practices?
We expressed to the BBB multiple times that if the situation wasn’t rectified, we would stop paying for accreditation and let our customers know why.
After a lot of waiting and no action at all from the BBB, we officially ended our relationship and will no longer pay for BBB accreditation.
We hope our services and happy customers reflect what type of business we are….and that we don’t need any special logo or stickers to prove it.

data.title: AI comes up with bizarre physics experiments, but they work
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了人工智能（AI）在实验物理学中的创新应用。加州理工学院的物理学家Rana Adhikari及其团队利用AI软件优化引力波探测器LIGO的设计，旨在提高其灵敏度，探测更广泛频率的引力波。尽管最初AI提出的设计看似复杂且不合常理，但经过整理和分析，研究人员发现AI通过增加一个三公里长的环来循环光线，从而减少量子噪声。这一设计能使LIGO的灵敏度提高10%到15%。AI的创新思路帮助科学家突破了传统方法的局限，展示了其在科学发现中的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在科学优化算法中的应用及其描述的准确性

不同观点：
• **LeroyRaz**：认为文章具有误导性，描述中的语言不准确。文章将优化算法描述为AI使用了深奥的理论和技巧，但实际上只是优化算法在人类编码的模拟空间中进行搜索，没有涉及到AI的概念操作或直觉。这种描述会让人误解为是更复杂的AI技术，而实际上只是经典的优化算法。
• **sampo**：指出过去这种优化算法不会被称为AI，但现在却被如此称呼。文章提到的Urania算法是一种高度并行化的混合局部-全局优化算法，本质上仍是优化算法，而非大众理解的AI。
• **JimDabell**：提到NASA曾经使用遗传算法进化天线，类似于文中的工作。这表明AI在生成更好解决方案方面有潜力，即使我们不完全理解其原因。
• **luketaylor**：认为在当前大家普遍误解AI为基于Transformer的语言模型的情况下，将这种优化程序称为AI是不严谨的。
• **markasoftware**：澄清文中的"AI"不是大型语言模型（LLM），而是基于梯度下降和拓扑优化的算法。
• **viraptor**：将文中的工作与NASA的进化天线类比，指出AI在某些情况下可以生成更好的结果，即使我们不完全理解其背后的原因。
• **topspin**：关注文章中提到的技术细节，如延迟线，并讨论其具体实现和作用。

补充讨论：
• **WhyNotHugo**：提出文章中隐含的社会现象，即人类过于离经叛道的想法往往被忽视，而AI提出的类似设计却被认真对待。
• **matt3210**：强调文中的"AI"只是一种并行优化算法，与当前流行的语言模型（如Claude、Grok、OpenAI）不同。
• **codeaether**：指出当前"AI"一词多指神经网络模型，甚至卷积神经网络都不再被视为"真正的AI"，这反映了公众对AI理解的变化。
• **anonym00se1**：预测未来会有更多类似标题的新闻，强调AI带来的新奇解决方案。
• **aeternum**：认为文章更多是炒作，实际上的AI只是重新发现了多年前俄罗斯科学家找到的技术，并进行了优化。
• **eleveriven**：对AI在科学方法中的新角色感到既兴奋又担忧，认为这是一个值得关注的趋势。
• **k__**：通过比较AI生成的设计与人类设计的不同，指出AI在处理边缘情况时的优势，建议从中学习。
• **smj-edison**：对文章中提到的量子模拟空间和算法优化工作表示兴趣，并希望了解其计算强度。

争议焦点：
• 文章中对AI的描述是否具有误导性，是否将传统的优化算法错误地归类为AI。
• 当前公众对AI的理解与实际技术实现之间的差距。
• AI在科学研究中的新角色及其对传统科学方法的潜在影响。

here are precision measurements, and then there’s the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory. In each of LIGO’s twin gravitational wave detectors (one in Hanford, Washington, and the other in Livingston, Louisiana), laser beams bounce back and forth down the four-kilometer arms of a giant L. When a gravitational wave passes through, the length of one arm changes relative to the other by less than the width of a proton. It’s by measuring these minuscule differences — a sensitivity akin to sensing the distance to the star Alpha Centauri down to the width of a human hair — that discoveries are made.
The design of the machine was decades in the making, as physicists needed to push every aspect to its absolute physical limits. Construction began in 1994 and took more than 20 years, including a four-year shutdown to improve the detectors, before LIGO detected its first gravitational wave in 2015: a ripple in the space-time fabric coming from the faraway collision of a pair of black holes.
Rana Adhikari
, a physicist at the California Institute of Technology, led the detector optimization team in the mid-2000s. He and a handful of collaborators painstakingly honed parts of the LIGO design, exploring the contours of every limit that stood in the way of a more sensitive machine.
But after the 2015 detection, Adhikari wanted to see if they could improve upon LIGO’s design, enabling it, for instance, to pick up gravitational waves in a broader band of frequencies. Such an improvement would enable LIGO to see merging black holes of different sizes, as well as potential surprises. “What we’d really like to discover is the wild new astrophysical thing no one has imagined,” Adhikari said. “We should have no prejudice about what the universe makes.”

Rana Adhikari, a physicist at the California Institute of Technology, recently employed AI to find ways of improving the design of gravitational-wave detectors.
Steve Babuljak
He and his team turned to AI — in particular, a software suite first created by the physicist Mario Krenn to design tabletop experiments in quantum optics. First, they gave the AI all the components and devices that could be mixed and matched to construct an arbitrarily complicated interferometer. The AI started off unconstrained. It could design a detector that spanned hundreds of kilometers and had thousands of elements, such as lenses, mirrors and lasers.
Initially, the AI’s designs seemed outlandish. “The outputs that the thing was giving us were really not comprehensible by people,” Adhikari said. “They were too complicated, and they looked like alien things or AI things. Just nothing that a human being would make, because it had no sense of symmetry, beauty, anything. It was just a mess.”
The researchers figured out how to clean up the AI’s outputs to produce interpretable ideas. Even so, the researchers were befuddled by the AI’s design. “If my students had tried to give me this thing, I would have said, ‘No, no, that’s ridiculous,’” Adhikari said. But the design was clearly effective.
It took months of effort to understand
what the AI was doing
. It turned out that the machine had used a counterintuitive trick to achieve its goals. It added an additional three-kilometer-long ring between the main interferometer and the detector to circulate the light before it exited the interferometer’s arms. Adhikari’s team realized that the AI was probably using some esoteric theoretical principles that Russian physicists had identified decades ago to reduce quantum mechanical noise. No one had ever pursued those ideas experimentally. “It takes a lot to think this far outside of the accepted solution,” Adhikari said. “We really needed the AI.”
AI software conceived of a novel layout of optical components that would make the LIGO gravitational-wave detectors 10 to 15% more sensitive. The aerial view shows the detector in Livingston, Louisiana.
Caltech/MIT/LIGO Lab

• bchris4：认为左撇子比例较高的地区多为思想更进步的区域，家长和老师不 discourage 左撇子行为。他对文章没有提到这一点感到意外。
• deathanatos：指出archive.org链接未能捕捉到原文内容，并提供了另一个存档链接。

• Supermancho：分享了自己从右撇子转为左撇子的个人经历，并提到家族中没有其他左撇子，可能暗示了环境对利手选择的影响。
• xrayarx：引用文章内容，指出20世纪80年代《国家地理》的气味测试是研究左撇子数据的一个奇怪来源，对此表示惊讶。

data.author: tolerance
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个技术工具或平台的功能、现状及macOS文件系统和系统Ruby的相关讨论。

不同观点：
• latexr认为该工具看起来已经被废弃，指出其缺乏关键更新（如未包含jq）且近期没有提交和问题进展，显示出该项目可能缺乏维护。
• qalmakka对macOS文件系统的目录结构表达不满，认为其混合了UNIX目录和Classic目录，尤其质疑/usr和/sbin等目录的存在，认为这些可以整合进/System以保持整洁。
• ysleepy希望工具能够提供更深层次的自动化分析功能，如XPC端点分析及二进制文件引用情况，并对这些信息是否能通过静态工具获取表示关注。
• Igrom提出一个功能建议，希望能够将所有二进制文件按字母顺序列在一个页面上，以便于查找。
• burnt-resistor提到工具在处理/System/Library下某些二进制文件时存在问题，给出具体例子（如Automator Installer和webdavfs_agent），指出这些文件信息无法准确获取。
• evolve2k对工具表示赞赏，分享了其使用工具查找系统Ruby的经历，但同时指出系统Ruby版本过旧对开发者（尤其是初学者）造成困扰，并询问系统Ruby存在的原因及背景。

补充讨论：
• 该工具的功能和现状是讨论的核心，其中latexr和burnt-resistor指出工具的不足和局限性，而ysleepy和Igrom则提出了功能改进建议。
• macOS文件系统的设计引起qalmakka的不满，特别是对Classic和UNIX目录混合使用提出批评。
• evolve2k对系统Ruby的讨论引发了对macOS中包含过时软件版本的开发者体验问题的关注，并希望获得更多背景信息。

争议焦点：
• 该工具是否仍被积极维护（latexr的观点）与其他用户对其功能的期待和改进建议（如ysleepy和Igrom）形成一定对比。
• macOS文件系统目录结构的合理性，特别是混合使用UNIX和Classic目录的做法，引发qalmakka的质疑。

data.title: Nasa’s X-59 quiet supersonic aircraft begins taxi tests
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: NASA的X-59静音超音速研究飞机于2025年7月10日在加利福尼亚州帕姆代尔的美国空军42号工厂进行了首次低速滑行测试，标志着这架独特的实验飞机首次在自身动力下移动。由NASA试飞员Nils Larson和来自NASA及洛克希德·马丁公司的团队共同完成，滑行测试是首飞前的最后一轮地面测试。在接下来的几周内，飞机将逐渐增加速度，最终进行高速滑行测试。低速测试中，工程师和机组人员监测飞机在跑道上的操控情况，验证转向和刹车等关键系统，确保其稳定性和控制性。X-59是NASA Quesst任务的核心，旨在通过将巨响的音爆减少为轻声的“砰”声，展示静音超音速飞行。测试数据将提供给美国及国际监管机构，为制定超音速商用飞行的新噪音标准提供依据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NASA的新型超音速飞机及其相关技术和商业可行性

不同观点：
• amendegree认为，NASA此举是为了提升公关形象，获取更多关注。
• boguscoder关注飞机前部重量分布，对降落程序是否需要更精细的操作表示好奇。
• widforss担心飞行员的视野问题，质疑飞机是否依赖摄像头或自动驾驶技术。
• HPsquared对飞机前部的大量空气动力学表面如何保持稳定性表示关注。
• erikerikson质疑超音速飞行的商业可行性和可持续性，怀疑是否仅为实验项目。
• NooneAtAll3提醒大家，NASA的X-59与Boom Airspace的XB-1是不同的项目，分别测试不同的技术。
• kaptainscarlet建议使用Starship，认为速度更快，但价格是主要障碍。
• wkat4242对安静的超音速滑行技术表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了不同项目的技术差异，如NASA的X-59和Boom Airspace的XB-1，这表明公众对不同技术的理解和关注点有所不同。
• 有人对商业可行性提出质疑，显示出对超音速飞行技术在实际应用中的可持续性和经济性的关注。
• 技术细节如飞机的重量分布、稳定性、视野和滑行噪音等也是讨论的重点，表明公众对飞机设计和操作的实际问题有浓厚兴趣。
• 不同评论之间存在潜在的争议焦点在于技术的实际可行性和应用前景，特别是商业航空的可持续性问题。

44615033.article_content:
2 min read
NASA’s X-59 Quiet Supersonic Aircraft Begins Taxi Tests
Nicolas Cholula
NASA Armstrong Public Affairs Specialist
Jul 17, 2025
Image Article
NASA/Jacob Shaw
NASA’s X-59 quiet supersonic research aircraft has officially begun taxi tests, marking the first time this one-of-a-kind experimental aircraft has moved under its own power.
NASA test pilot Nils Larson and the X-59 team, made up of NASA and contractor Lockheed Martin personnel, completed the aircraft’s first low-speed taxi test at U.S. Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale, California, on July 10, 2025.
The taxiing represents the X-59’s last series of ground tests before first flight. Over the coming weeks, the aircraft will gradually increase its speed, leading up to a high-speed taxi test that will take the aircraft just short of the point where it would take off.
During the low-speed tests, engineers and flight crews monitored how the X-59 handled as it moved across the runway, working to validate critical systems like steering and braking. These checks help ensure the aircraft’s stability and control across a range of conditions, giving pilots and engineers confidence that all systems are functioning as expected.
The X-59 is the centerpiece of NASA’s
Quesst mission
, which aims to demonstrate quiet supersonic flight by reducing the loud sonic boom to a quieter “thump.” Data gathered from the X-59 will be shared with U.S. and international regulators to inform the establishment of new, data-driven acceptable noise thresholds related to supersonic commercial flight over land.
NASA’s X-59 quiet supersonic research aircraft taxis across the runway during a low-speed taxi test at U.S. Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale, California, on July 10, 2025. The test marks the start of taxi tests and the last series of ground tests before first flight.
NASA/Carla Thomas
NASA’s X-59 quiet supersonic research aircraft moves under its own power for the first time at Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works facility in Palmdale, California, on July 10, 2025. Guided by the aircraft’s crew chief, the event marks the beginning of taxi tests – a key milestone and the final series of ground tests before first flight.
NASA/Carla Thomas

data.title: A brief history of primary coding languages
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文简要回顾了苹果开发语言的演变历史。最初，Lisa电脑使用Lisa Pascal及其扩展版Clascal进行开发。1986年，Object Pascal成为Mac开发的主要语言，配合MacApp库，广泛用于应用开发，如Adobe Photoshop。1991年，随着System 7发布，苹果转向C/C++，导致许多开发者面临挑战。随后，Metrowerks的CodeWarrior成为主流开发环境。2001年，Mac OS X引入Objective-C，取代C++，成为新的主要开发语言。2014年，Swift发布，逐渐取代Objective-C，成为苹果新的主力开发语言，提供多范式编程支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Objective-C与Swift的比较以及历史上的开发语言演变

不同观点：
• spacedcowboy认为Objective-C（ObjC）相比Swift认知负担更小，因为Swift每年都在重新设计，导致在线查找示例代码变得困难。他还指出，ObjC在语言设计上只是对C增加了约两个 dozen 的关键词，并通过ARC管理内存，与C和C++有良好的集成。他表示尽管Apple正在逐渐转向Swift，但由于内部大量代码仍是ObjC，完全放弃对ObjC的支持还需要很长时间。spacedcowboy还提到自己正在开发一个跨平台的项目，以摆脱对Swift的依赖。

• duskwuff则回顾了Mac开发的早期历史，指出最初的官方开发语言是Pascal，而不是任何面向对象的语言。他提到早期的Mac文档和Toolbox程序都假设开发者使用Pascal，并且大多数例程都采用Pascal字符串作为参数。

补充讨论：
• spacedcowboy对Swift的批评主要集中在其频繁的变化和与ObjC相比的复杂性上，同时他也承认Apple不太可能完全放弃对ObjC的支持。
• duskwuff的评论则提供了关于开发语言历史演变的背景信息，帮助理解ObjC和Swift出现之前的情况。
• spacedcowboy还提到自己正在进行的跨平台项目，并提供了项目的链接，显示出对技术自主和跨平台解决方案的强烈兴趣。

争议焦点：Swift的频繁变化和复杂性是否超过了其带来的好处，以及开发者是否应该继续依赖ObjC而非完全转向Swift。

44613361.article_content:
Plenty of great apps have been created using the Mac’s
scripting languages
, but commercial developers have largely relied on compiled languages used and supported by Apple for app and system development. Over the years those have included Object Pascal, C/C++, Objective-C and most recently Swift. This article provides a brief overview of how those changed.
Lisa Clascal (1984-86)
Following Apple’s use of UCSD Pascal on Apple II computers, when the Lisa was being developed its primary language was Lisa Pascal. Apple was also working on the novel object-oriented language Smalltalk which originated in Xerox’s PARC in 1969, but its syntax was unfamiliar and performance was poor. Lisa Pascal was therefore developed into Clascal, dividing code into distinct interface and implementation sections, with classes, subclasses, methods and inheritance.
During the first couple of years, software for the Mac was thus developed using Clascal on Lisa systems.
Object Pascal (1986-91)
In 1984-85, Larry Tesler and supporting engineers in Apple (including Barry Haynes, Ken Doyle and Larry Rosenstein) worked with Niklaus Wirth, the inventor of Pascal, to develop Clascal into Object Pascal, the primary language for Mac development. With this, they also developed the first version of the MacApp class library that provided a framework to support common application features including the Mac’s GUI.
These were released together in September 1986, in Macintosh Programmer’s Workshop (MPW), which was adopted as the standard development environment for the Mac, both in-house and for third-parties. At that time, the only compiled language supported by MPW was Object Pascal, and it wasn’t until the following summer that the first beta of its C/C++ compiler was released with MPW 2.0. That was developed by Greenhills, but Object Pascal remained the more widely used, particularly in combination with MacApp, also written in Object Pascal. Major developers including Adobe created early versions of their products using Object Pascal and MacApp, perhaps the most famous example being Adobe Photoshop.
At the same time, Think Technologies released the first popular third-party compiler, LightSpeed C, in 1986. This soon became THINK C, gained C++ support, was joined by THINK Pascal, and was bought by Symantec. Borland ported its Turbo Pascal to the Mac, where it adopted the extensions of Object Pascal, and eventually became the cross-platform Delphi in 1995.
C/C++ (1991-2001)
With the release of System 7 in 1991, Apple abruptly switched from Object Pascal to C++, and MacApp 3.0 also changed language. Smaller developers who had extensive source in Object Pascal were far from happy, and in some cases successful products vanished from the market. Others were rescued when Metrowerks released a new integrated development environment for C/C++ as CodeWarrior at the end of 1993 or early 1994. This drew most who had been using THINK C, and MPW also went into decline. The decisive factor was CodeWarrior’s early support for Apple’s new PowerPC Macs. CodeWarrior’s C/C++ saw many Mac developers through that hardware transition until the release of Mac OS X in 2000-01.
Objective-C (2001-)
With Mac OS X came its own primary development language Objective-C, and Apple’s new integrated development environment Project Builder, also derived from NeXTSTEP but written from scratch for the Mac. That was replaced by the first version of Xcode with Mac OS X 10.3 Panther in 2003.
This screenshot shows Xcode in 2015.
Objective-C had been one of the two object-oriented contenders to succeed C. The other, C++, had already become more widely adopted, and had been favoured by Apple for the previous decade. Although both claim C as their ancestor, there’s little in common between them, and in many respects Objective-C more closely resembles Smalltalk, rejected by Apple when developing the Lisa. Developers whose source code had started in Object Pascal and was then ported to C++, had another major task to convert that to Objective-C.
Originally designed and developed by Brad Cox and Tom Love during the early 1980s, Objective-C’s biggest success had been its selection as the primary development language for NeXTSTEP later that decade. When Apple adopted that as the foundation for Mac OS X, it was inevitable that the language should come with it.
Swift (2014-)
In keeping with its track record, no sooner had Apple entered the 2010s than its engineers, under the lead of Chris Lattner, were working on the successor to Objective-C. Significant early collaborators included Doug Gregor, John McCall, Ted Kremenek and Joe Groff. A first beta-release was provided at WWDC in 2014, and since then Swift has been progressively replacing Objective-C as Apple’s primary development language.
Swift is described as being a multi-paradigm language, and over the course of the last 15 years it has assimilated and adopted almost every available programming paradigm, from classes and objects to protocols
44613361.article_summary: 本文简要回顾了苹果开发语言的演变历史。最初，Lisa电脑使用Lisa Pascal及其扩展版Clascal进行开发。1986年，Object Pascal成为Mac开发的主要语言，配合MacApp库，广泛用于应用开发，如Adobe Photoshop。1991年，随着System 7发布，苹果转向C/C++，导致许多开发者面临挑战。随后，Metrowerks的CodeWarrior成为主流开发环境。2001年，Mac OS X引入Objective-C，取代C++，成为新的主要开发语言。2014年，Swift发布，逐渐取代Objective-C，成为苹果新的主力开发语言，提供多范式编程支持。

data.title: Bill to Restrict AI Companies Unauthorized Use of Copyrighted Works for Training
data.author: OutOfHere
data.article_summary: 参议员乔什·霍利（R-MO）和理查德·布鲁门撒尔（D-CT）提出了一项法案，旨在限制AI公司未经许可使用版权材料进行模型训练。该法案名为《AI问责与个人数据保护法》，允许个人对未经其明确事先同意而使用其个人数据或版权作品的公司提起诉讼。同时，法案要求公司在获得同意时披露将访问数据的三方。该立法回应了科技公司与内容所有者之间的争论，一些知名作家如约翰·格里森姆和乔治·R·R·马丁曾对此提出质疑，而OpenAI等公司则主张这种使用属于合理使用。霍利表示，该法案旨在让创作者通过法律手段保护其作品和数据。布鲁门撒尔则强调，科技公司必须为其侵犯消费者隐私的行为承担法律责任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于政治人物支持某项行动的讨论，涉及版权法、数据隐私以及知识产权（IP）的争议。

不同观点：
• [nunez] 认为大型跨党派政治人物围绕这一行动团结起来是令人欣喜的现象，并对这一跨党派努力表示惊讶。这表明该行动得到了广泛的政治支持。

• [CaptainFever] 指出这实际上是版权法的扩展，并提醒人们当前的版权法已经非常严格，尤其是其长达100年的保护期限，暗示该行动可能进一步加剧版权限制。

• [Frieren] 强调了在未经明确同意的情况下，使用个人数据来训练模型的问题，认为这种行为不仅仅是法律责任，还具有一种反乌托邦和赛博朋克的味道，暗示对隐私和数据滥用的担忧。

• [pyman] 通过类比（Poogle公司）的方式，批评微软、Google等公司支持的所谓“公平使用”原则，实际上是知识产权的盗窃行为。他主张公司应记录用于训练模型的每一本书、文章、照片或视频，并在生成新内容时对版权持有人进行补偿，反对将机器学习模型视为不可解释的黑箱。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于版权法的扩展和知识产权的使用，特别是涉及数据隐私和模型训练的合法性问题。
• pyman 的评论尤其指出了科技公司在使用数据和训练模型时的透明性和补偿问题，认为当前的做法是不公平的。
• Frieren 和 pyman 的观点都涉及了对个人数据和知识产权保护的关注，但前者更侧重于隐私和道德问题，而后者则聚焦于法律和经济补偿。

总的来说，讨论围绕着政治支持、版权法扩展、数据隐私和知识产权的合法性及道德性问题展开。

Sen.

(D-CT) introduced legislation on Monday that would restrict
AI
companies from using copyrighted material in their training models without the consent of the individual owner.
The
AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act
also would allow individuals to sue companies that uses their personal data or copyrighted works without their “express, prior consent.”

The bill addresses a raging debate between tech and content owners, one that has already led to extensive litigation. Companies like OpenAI have argued that the use of copyrighted materials in training models is a fair use, while figures including John Grisham and George R.R. Martin have challenged that notion.
In a statement, Hawley said, “AI companies are robbing the American people blind while leaving artists, writers, and other creators with zero recourse. It’s time for Congress to give the American worker their day in court to protect their personal data and creative works.”
Watch on Deadline
Blumenthal said, “Tech companies must be held accountable—and liable legally—when they breach consumer privacy, collecting, monetizing or sharing personal information without express consent. Consumers must be given rights and remedies—and legal tools to make them real—not relying on government enforcement alone.”
The bill also requires companies to disclose third parties that will access data once consent is sought.

data.title: NASA loses another senior official as tension about the agency's future grows
data.author: xqcgrek2
data.article_summary: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center director Makenzie Lystrup announced her resignation on July 21, 2025, effective August 1, following the recent departure of NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory director Laurie Leshin. Their exits come amid significant federal budget cuts and personnel reductions, with over 2,000 senior employees set to leave. These cuts, proposed by President Trump, target NASA’s space and Earth science programs and include phasing out the Space Launch System and Orion spacecraft. More than 280 current and former NASA staff signed a letter opposing the budget changes, warning of "catastrophic impacts" to the agency’s mission. Lystrup’s resignation reason was not disclosed, but internal turmoil and workforce cuts are speculated to play a role. Cynthia Simmons will replace Lystrup as acting director.

主要讨论点：NASA高层人员离职及其与政府行政干预的关系

不同观点：
• [hn-throwaway998] 认为JPL主任Lauy Leshin的辞职与政府内部政治斗争有关。该评论指出Leshin与政府不和，并暗示她因为不愿服从当前政府的绝对控制而被迫辞职。此外，该评论提到前代理署长Janet Petro的离职也是出于类似原因，暗示当前政府倾向于任命顺从的人士担任关键职位，目的是为了加强对机构的控制，最终可能导致整个机构的崩溃。

• [dimator] 表达了对NASA现状的悲痛，认为这是当前政府领导下最令人遗憾的灾难性结果之一。评论强调NASA作为一个顶级科学和探索机构，多年来对社会的巨大贡献，但现在却面临着被削弱和解体的危机。该评论质疑这种做法的目的和价值，暗示对政府行为的不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于NASA高层人员离职是否确实由于政府行政干预和政治斗争。一方认为这是明显的政治操作，目的是清除不顺从的领导层；另一方则对此表示极度遗憾和不解，认为这种行为是在破坏一个对社会有巨大贡献的机构。

• [hn-throwaway998] 提到了具体的个人，如Leshin和Petro，认为她们的离职与政府的不满有关，并推测新上任的代理署长是“顺从”的人，暗示人事变动背后有政治动机。

• [dimator] 没有具体提及个人，但更关注NASA整体作为一个科学和探索机构的命运，对当前局势感到悲愤，认为这种变化是在“摧毁”NASA的核心价值和贡献。

总的来说，评论者一致认为NASA正面临严重的管理问题，但讨论的重点在于这些问题的根源是否在于政府对机构的控制和干预。

The director of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center announced her resignation Monday, marking yet another high-profile departure as questions loom about the agency’s budget and future.
Makenzie Lystrup, who has served as director of the center in Maryland since April 2023, will leave the agency on Aug. 1,
according to a NASA statement
. Goddard oversees a number of key NASA missions, including the Hubble Space Telescope, the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the OSIRIS-REx mission that collected samples from an asteroid.
Lystrup’s resignation comes less than two months after Laurie Leshin stepped down as director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, California.
Makenzie Lystrup, director of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, during a panel discussion at the 2024 Artemis Suppliers Conference in Washington, D.C.
Joel Kowsky / NASA
The departures are playing out as NASA and other government agencies contend with
significant cuts to funding and personnel
, as part of a broader push to shrink the size of the federal workforce. Questions are swirling internally at NASA and
on Capitol Hill
about how the space agency can accomplish its work with far fewer personnel and why such cuts are moving ahead before Congress has authorized the agency’s budget.
Meanwhile, more than 2,000 senior-level employees are set to leave NASA as part of an effort to cut the agency’s workforce, as was
first reported by Politico
. Those include people in senior positions of management and individuals with specialized skills, Politico reported, raising concerns about a “brain drain” at the space agency.
Workers at the space agency have until Friday to accept “deferred resignations,” buyouts or early retirement offers.
President Donald Trump’s proposed budget for 2026 would slash about 25%, or more than $6 billion, from NASA’s budget. The steepest cuts would come out of the agency’s space science, Earth science and mission support divisions,
according to the budget blueprint
.
If enacted by Congress, the budget would also phase out NASA's
Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft
, which the agency was developing to return astronauts to the moon.
In response to the budget blueprint, more than 280 current and former NASA employees signed a letter to Sean Duffy, NASA’s interim administrator, stating that the Trump administration’s recent policies “have or threaten to waste public resources, compromise human safety, weaken national security, and undermine the core NASA mission.”
The letter, known as the
Voyager Declaration
, said the changes have caused “catastrophic impacts” to the agency’s workforce, and have “prioritized political momentum over human safety, scientific advancement, and efficient use of public resources.”
Before Duffy replaced NASA’s previous acting administrator, Janet Petro, employees pressed her to explain how the budget cuts and restructuring underway served the best interests of the space agency, according to internal correspondence read by NBC News.
It’s not clear if Lystrup and Leshin’s departures are related to the ongoing turmoil at NASA and other government agencies. In
NASA’s announcement about Leshin’s resignation
, it said she was stepping down “for personal reasons.”
The agency did not provide a reason for Lystrup’s resignation. In an internal email obtained by NBC News, Lystrup said she leaves with “confidence” in the Goddard’s leadership team “and all of you who will shape the next chapter of this center.”
“I am honored to have been part of this incredible journey with you,” she wrote in the email. “It has been my privilege.”
NASA said Monday that Cynthia Simmons, Goddard's deputy director, will take over as acting center director in August.
Denise Chow
Denise Chow is a science and space reporter for NBC News.
Lora Kolodny, CNBC
Julia Jester
Julia Jester is a producer for NBC News based in Washington, D.C.
Jonathan Allen
Jonathan Allen is a senior national politics reporter for NBC News.

data.author: hammyhavoc
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了生成式AI在电子游戏领域的局限性，特别是针对复古游戏的创作。尽管AI在科学和医学等领域有一定应用，但公司在娱乐领域的过度炒作引发了质疑。文章批评了一些人（“AI兄弟”）过于乐观地认为AI能轻松制作出可玩的复古游戏，然而现有的AI连基本任务都难以胜任，更不用说复杂的游戏开发。作者强调，视频游戏作为艺术形式，承载着创作者的情感和经验，AI生成的内容缺乏这种人性化的特质。尽管有人如埃隆·马斯克宣称AI即将实现这一目标，但实际进展远未达到预期，且AI的不可控性和错误频出进一步暴露了其局限性。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44642654.article_content:
Image: Zion Grassl / Time Extension
If you value the human spirit's boundless creativity and resourcefulness, then the tiresome trend of
Generative AI
is probably getting on your nerves right now.
Sure, AI has its uses – it's already helping us gain enhanced understanding of the worlds of
science
and
medicine
, for example – but it seems companies like Meta, Google and OpenAI are more concerned with leveraging it to create
obnoxious slop
.
Just as 'AI bros' will insist that the worlds of movies, TV and music are on borrowed time now that AI is here, there are similar predictions being made about the world of video games. Indeed, we've already seen proof of concepts for
AI-created games
, none of which look like they'd be particularly enjoyable to play at the moment.
However, a couple of social media posts seem to have stirred the ant's nest recently, and both relate to using AI to create retro games – something that, in the mind of an AI bro, should be
really
simple, right? Retro games are old and basic, and surely there's nothing
too
complex about them. Game mechanics, narrative, art design, etc – none of these things matter when you have really good AI, right?
Right?
Retro games that don't exist
But I wish they did.
1. Lord of the Rings: 🧵
pic.twitter.com/OA3wPmzL2r
— Allen T. (@Mr_AllenT)
July 19, 2025
Unfortunately for the AI bros,
the 'examples' shown in this thread
prove that getting an AI to spit out a video approximation of what a retro game looks like in motion (based on millions of minutes of copyrighted footage,
most of which will have been used without permission
, I'll wager) is an almost unfathomable distance away from that same AI being able to create a working, cohesive (and playable) game.
None of this pie-in-the-sky thinking should surprise us, of course; if you were being
especially
unkind, you could point out that the entire AI industry is built on
hype
– the classic example of
over-promising to keep people interested
, and then moving the goalposts when you realise you can't achieve what you said was possible. Somewhat predictably, the undisputed king of such activity,
Elon Musk
, has waded into this debate and seems confident that we're "close" to getting an AI to create retro games from scratch (specifically SNES games). I'm assuming he typed those words with a serious face, but I'm not
totally
sure.
Of course, Musk has also predicted in the past that we'd have
a million Robotaxis on the streets by 2020
, and that you'd be able to take the Hyperloop from LA to San Fransico in 30 minutes (
spoiler alert: you can't
). Oh, and he said we'd have a colony on Mars in this decade.
He's not the most reliable of people when it comes to this kind of thing, you see.
We’re pretty close
@xAI
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk)
July 20, 2025
That Musk and his AI acolytes honestly believe that AI is going to be capable of creating a half-decent video game any time soon is a joke in itself; the tech has proven it's unworthy of even basic tasks at present,
and has been in the headlines for making glaring errors
. Furthermore, many AI experts are
now admitting that it's hard to understand or even control what an AI is doing
. How can it possibly be expected to produce something as complex and multi-faceted as a piece of interactive entertainment, even one designed for a console that's almost 40 years old? Heck,
AI can't even beat a 48-year-old Atari 2600 chess program without cheating.
But, let's say for one second that a computer, with minimal prompt-based input from a human,
could
perform such a task to an acceptable standard –
why on earth would you want it to?
Video games, like all art forms, carry an imprint of the human beings who made them. They're not created in the emotionless silicon vacuum of a GPU following a few loose prompts, but forged in the hearts, minds and experiences of real people – people with hopes, fears, dreams, expectations and much more. I honestly can't think of anything more depressing than playing a video game made by using AI (
granted, modern-day AAA game development can
sometimes
make it feel that way
).
The notion of such a piece of software being able to balance the massive creative and coding demands of game development without
serious
human intervention is not just a massive insult to the medium of interactive entertainment, but it's also nothing but a pipe dream – but then, when you've got something to sell, you make
damn
sure you hype it to high heaven.
News
Google's Gemini AI Assistant Is Pretty Awful At Video Game History
We're not out of the job quite yet
Feature
ChatGPT Translated An Article About Space Harrier, Then Suggested "Tailoring" It For Retro Gamer
The threat of Generative AI is very real
News
OpenAI's ChatGPT Lost A Game Of Chess Against The 48-Year-Old Atari 2600
"ChatGPT got absolutely wrecked on the beginner level"

data.title: What will become of the CIA?
data.author: Michelangelo11
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了1988年苏联解体前夕，美国中情局（CIA）的苏联问题专家们在参议员比尔·布拉德利召集的闭门会议上表达了对苏联解体后自身职业前景的忧虑。随着苏联的消失，这些以分析苏联为生的专家感到前途未卜。随后，美国在冷战后放松了警惕，中情局预算被削减，特工撤离。克林顿总统上任后专注于经济问题，与中情局互动甚少。直到90年代末，基地组织发动一系列恐怖袭击，美国才重新重视情报工作。在9/11事件后，中情局迅速展开反击行动，但内部存在冒险的行动派与谨慎的分析派之间的矛盾。记者蒂姆·韦纳在其新书中详细记录了这些历史事件，并探讨了中情局在21世纪面临的挑战和其历史遗留问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对美国情报机构（CIA及整个IC）的角色、行为和影响的评价与争议

不同观点：
• **CIA的权力与秘密行动**：
  - [cuuupid] 指出CIA在很大程度上掌控并指导着整个情报体系（IC），包括网络、卫星和无人机等基础设施，甚至通过设立新的秘密情报机构规避国会监督。这表明CIA拥有过大的权力且缺乏有效监督。
  - [jxf] 认为，即便对美国情报机构有不满，系统性地削弱国家治理能力是一个更严重的问题，暗示CIA在国家安全中的作用不可或缺。

• **CIA行为的正当性与道德问题**：
  - [jonyt] 批评文章对9/11事件的分析，认为作者对本·拉登动机的解读过于牵强，本·拉登作为恐怖分子的目标是建立哈里发，而非简单的道德打击。
  - [hackandthink] 认为即便揭露了情报机构的错误和罪行，但如果这些组织被废除，世界会变得更好，暗示CIA的存在本身是负面影响。

• **情报工作的本质与局限**：
  - [Animats] 强调情报工作能够提供敌方能力的信息，但难以判断其意图，尤其是在和平时期，决策者往往希望情报能预测未来，但这通常很难实现。

• **CIA与政治的关系**：
  - [jokoon] 提出一个哲学问题，即如果一个民选领导人背叛国家，是否算作叛国。同时指出，CIA受白宫指挥，因此其行动本质上与政治密不可分。
  - [caseysoftware] 质疑文章是否在为CIA辩护，指出文章罗列了CIA几十年来的失败，并批评文章将CIA与民选领导对立起来的描述。

• **CIA的历史罪行与阴谋论**：
  - [cess11] 提到CIA在全球毒品贸易中的角色，特别是与意大利黑手党的联系，认为这些历史罪行常常被忽视。
  - [gadders] 认为文章未能经受住时间考验，并提到有关CIA与奥巴马政府在特朗普与俄罗斯勾结问题上的阴谋论。

补充讨论：
• **CIA的形象与文化影响**：
  - [ggm] 提到非美国视角下对CIA的负面看法，指出像詹姆斯·邦德系列中的CIA角色Felix Leiter是少有的正面形象。
  - [reginald78] 讽刺地提到CIA通过非法手段（如贩卖毒品）自我资助的问题。

• **对CIA的怀疑态度**：
  - [NoelJacob] 简单直接地表达对CIA的怀疑，暗示文章可能是CIA的宣传。

争议焦点：
• CIA的权力是否过大，尤其是在规避国会监督方面。
• CIA行为的正当性，特别是在涉及战争、干涉选举和全球犯罪活动等问题上。
• 情报工作的本质局限与决策者期望之间的矛盾。
• CIA与民选政府的关系以及其在民主制度中的角色。
